official.deadline_note: Deadlines are the same for CSS Profile, FAFSA and IDOC: Restrictive Early Action and QuestBridge Match 1 November; Regular Decision 1 February; Transfer 1 March. Enrolled students renew by 1 May and receive notification by 1 July. A late application carries no penalty or reduction in aid, but the aid decision may be delayed.
official.application_cycle: 2027-2028 school year (prospective applicants for fall 2027 entry)
official.status_note: The College's published aid instructions state: 'The instructions below are for the 2027-2028 school year.' Aid applications are accepted alongside the admission application for the current cycle.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Published wording: '$100,000 family income and below, with typical assets: Free - Financial aid covers all billed expenses, including tuition, fees, food, housing, and more.' And: '$200,000 family income and below, with typical assets: Free Tuition Plus - Financial aid covers the full cost of tuition, plus.'

official.application_route: No separate award application: submit the CSS Profile (and IDOC documents, plus FAFSA for US citizens/permanent residents) alongside the Common Application admission form by the admission-round deadline.
official.citizenship_residency: Application instructions apply regardless of country of residence or citizenship status; financial aid is available to foreign students on exactly the same basis as for American students, but foreign students cannot receive federal funding.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - international students are eligible for exactly the same aid as American students, with the same application process, documents and deadlines. They are excluded from federal aid (Pell Grant, SEOG, Federal Work-Study, federal loans) but can receive Harvard scholarship, Harvard student employment and the Harvard Loan.
official.duration: Four-year residential undergraduate program; aid is awarded for one academic year and re-applied for and re-awarded annually.
official.description: The Griffin Financial Aid Office provides need-based aid that allows Harvard to bring the best students regardless of their ability to pay, aided by Ken Griffin's transformative generosity. Financial aid is available to foreign students on exactly the same basis as for American students, with the College applying its own job and scholarship money.
official.program_type: Need-based undergraduate financial aid program (not a merit scholarship)

verification.notes: All figures and deadlines taken from Harvard College's own financial aid and admissions pages, fetched live. The $91,634 figure is the published 2026-27 subtotal of billed costs (tuition, fees, housing, food) that aid covers in full for families with income of $100,000 or below with typical assets; 2027-28 billed costs are not yet published.

applicant_utility.summary: Harvard College admits need-blind and meets 100% of demonstrated need for everyone who applies for aid, which makes it one of the only routes to a near-free Ivy League degree for applicants from any country. There is no separate scholarship form: you file the CSS Profile through the College Board at the same time you submit your admission application, and international families substitute their own country's tax paperwork for a US 1040. The dollar ceiling is set by your family's income and assets, not by your grades, so the win here comes from documenting an accurate financial picture early and filing by 1 November or 1 February. Budget for roughly the billed cost of attendance out of pocket if your family's income sits above the thresholds.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Students from modest or middle-income families anywhere in the world whose family income is at or below roughly $100,000 and who can produce translated tax or employer income documents.
application_readiness_checklist: Collect both parents' most recent filed national tax returns (or employer letters and pay slips if they do not file) before opening the CSS Profile
Decide the admission round first: CSS Profile, FAFSA and IDOC all share the 1 November Restrictive Early Action, 1 February Regular Decision or 1 March Transfer deadline
Create a College Board account, register the CSS Profile for Harvard under code 3434, and pay or request a fee waiver before the deadline
Prepare English translations of every non-English income document yourself or via a teacher - official translators are not needed
Gather business or farm tax returns and any trust documents in advance, since these are the most common reason an IDOC packet stalls
common_rejection_risks: Sending draft or estimated tax returns, which Harvard explicitly rejects in favor of the actual filed 2025 return
Emailing documents to the office instead of uploading them through IDOC; emailed materials are refused as insecure
Leaving out schedules and W-2 pages from a US tax return, which leaves the file incomplete without any warning to a prospective applicant
Parents filing a single CSS Profile when they are separated or divorced, or the reverse when they live together
Missing the Communication that the CSS Profile must be filed before IDOC will open, then running out of time before the deadline
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The expected student contribution: Harvard expects students to cover about $3,500 in personal expenses per academic year, normally met through term-time work of roughly 10-12 hours a week. Families above the income thresholds also pay a parent contribution, and health insurance costs $4,954 for 2026-27 unless the student is covered under a family plan.
document_audit: Canadian families must submit the T-1 General as the tax document and the T-2 Corporate for a business - a Canadian notice of assessment is not accepted
International students who use an HUID instead of an SSN on every form avoid a common mismatched-record delay
A full legal name (no nicknames) is required on CSS Profile and FAFSA submissions
A trust or estate beneficiary must supply both the full trust tax return and an explanatory letter about value and accessibility
alerts: Applying for aid never hurts admission chances, but a late aid application is processed after decisions are released and can leave an admitted international student unable to prove funds in time for a visa

Harvard does not track financial aid materials for prospective students until after admission, so a missing document may not surface until it is too late to fix - verify completeness through the College Board account instead
International applicants are not required to take an English proficiency exam for admission, but Visiting Undergraduate Program applicants must submit TOEFL or IELTS
Outside awards and scholarships you win elsewhere must be reported and will first replace your work expectation, then reduce your Harvard scholarship - they cannot reduce your parent contribution
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the Common Application with the aid indicator, file the CSS Profile (code 3434) and, for US citizens/permanent residents, the FAFSA (code E00468) by the round deadline, then upload every requested tax and business document through the College Board IDOC Service.
